chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when the last ten [days] entered, would tighten his gown, keep away from the women, revive the night [in prayer], and devote himself to worship.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad do during the last ten days of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) specific Sunnah of *I’tikaf* during the final ten days of Ramadan, emphasizing a shift from worldly engagements to exclusive spiritual devotion. The act of 'tightening the waistband' (*shadd al-mi'zar*) is traditionally interpreted by Shia scholars as a signal to his household to reduce distractions, ensuring a focused environment for night prayers and Quran recitation. This practice underscores the importance of maximizing worship during the nights when the Decree of the Year is determined, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theological understanding of Ramadan's blessings.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever the last days (of a Month of Ramazan) entered, would tighten the gown, and keep away from the women, and revive the night, and be free for the worship’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman from ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, during the last ten days of the month of Ramadan would prepare himself well, stay away from women, stay awake the whole night, and free himself for worship.’”
